terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the old import script and your tokenizer read the supplier lists.

tasks.title: Cut marks and words into tokens
tasks.description:
Implement `tokenize(text)` in `src/json.js` for texts made only of marks and words, with nothing between them.

- it returns an array of tokens, in the order they stand in the text
- each of the six marks `{` `}` `[` `]` `:` `,` is a token `{ type: 'mark', value, at, end }`, where `value` is the mark itself
- each of the words `true`, `false` and `null` is a token `{ type: 'literal', value, at, end }`, where `value` is the JavaScript value `true`, `false` or `null`, not the word
- `at` is the index of the token's first character and `end` the index just after its last one, so `text.slice(at, end)` is the token as written
- an empty text gives an empty array, and every call starts a new list

The check tokenizes texts of its own and compares every token's type, value, at and end.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and read the error under "Your tokenizer".
Start a list and an index at 0, and loop while the index is inside the text.
Look at the character at the index: is it one of the six marks? Push its token and move one on.
If not, is one of the three words written from here? Push its token and move past the whole word.
hints: Everything happens in one loop that walks the text with an index. Each time round, the character at the index decides what the next token is.
A mark is one character long, so its end is at + 1. A word is as long as the word, and its value comes from a small table from the word to the JavaScript value, so 'true' gives true.
`text.startsWith('true', i)` says whether the word starts at index i; then push `{ type: 'literal', value: true, at: i, end: i + 4 }` and add 4 to i.

tasks.title: Skip the space between tokens
tasks.description:
Make `tokenize(text)` skip the space between tokens.

- space, tab, line feed and carriage return between, before and after tokens are skipped and make no token
- `at` and `end` still count every character of the text, the skipped ones included
- a text of nothing but those four gives an empty array

The check tokenizes texts of its own with spaces, tabs and line breaks in many places and compares every token.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and look at the list over several lines.
In your loop, before you look for a mark or a word, check for one of the four space characters.
Move the index one on and go round again, without pushing anything.
hints: Skipping is just moving the index without making a token. Do it in the same loop, before the other checks.
Do not remove the space from the text first: the indexes of every token after it would shift, and at would point at the wrong place.
`if (' \t\n\r'.includes(ch)) { i++; continue }` near the top of the loop skips one space character.

tasks.title: Say where a stray character sits
tasks.description:
Make `tokenize(text)` throw when it meets a character that starts no token.

- it throws a `JsonError`, the class at the top of `src/json.js`, never another error and never by dropping the character
- the error's `at` is the index of that character, counted from the start of the text, from 0
- its message names the character and its index, such as `Unexpected character ' at index 194`
- a character that only looks like space, such as a no-break space or a form feed, starts no token either
- a word that is not exactly `true`, `false` or `null`, such as `True` or `nul`, throws too

The check gives `tokenize` texts with stray characters in different places and reads the error it throws.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js`: the last piece has a single quote, the card supplier's mistake.
Find the place in your loop where a character is neither space, nor a mark, nor the start of a word.
Throw a JsonError there with a message and the index.
Make sure nothing else in the loop skips characters it does not know.
hints: Your loop already knows every character that is allowed. Whatever reaches the end of the loop body without a match is the stray one.
Dropping the character and moving on would hide the very mistake Idris needs to hear about. And a loop that neither throws nor moves on never ends.
``throw new JsonError(`Unexpected character ${ch} at index ${i}`, i)`` at the end of the loop body.
